plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In the wild, the poinsettia is a tall, open shrub or small tree, not a tidy pot plant. It can reach 3–4 metres. Its fiery crimson bracts, which are leaf-like and often mistaken for petals, blaze above the dry winter landscape. The tiny yellow true flowers sit in the centre of each cluster.
plants.bloomingSeason: December, in the dry winter season
plants.location: Mexico and Central America, where it grows wild
plants.funFact: The showy red parts are modified leaves, not petals. They change colour in response to the long nights of late autumn, and that is why poinsettias are linked with the holidays.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens silky, lightly scented blossoms just as most gardens go quiet. The flowers are single or semi-double and have a golden boss of stamens. They shower the ground with petals like confetti on cool early-winter days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October or November through December and into January)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan, and widely grown in temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: It is one of the earliest camellias to bloom. Its relative, Camellia sinensis, gives us tea.

plants.name: Agapanthus campanulatus
plants.description: Long, slender stalks carry rounded clusters of 10 to 30 bell-shaped flowers in pale to deep blue, each petal marked with a darker stripe. They nod above arching, strap-like leaves, and they open as southern-hemisphere summer begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (December to March)
plants.location: Grasslands and rocky slopes of South Africa
plants.funFact: Its genus name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'. Despite the common name 'African lily', it belongs to the amaryllis family.
